title.value: Model-based graph reinforcement learning for inductive traffic signal control
title.justification: The title clearly summarizes the focus of the paper, which is on using model-based reinforcement learning combined with graph neural networks for traffic signal control.
title.quote: Model-based graph reinforcement learning for inductive traffic signal control

extractions.description: The paper introduces MuJAM, a model-based reinforcement learning method for adaptive traffic signal control (ATSC). The approach uses graph neural networks to handle changing inputs and environments, facilitating zero-shot transfer to new road-network topologies and traffic distributions.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on minimizing traffic congestion, which is linked to environmental and social impacts. It promotes adaptive traffic signal control, which can contribute to reducing these impacts as part of broader climate change mitigation tactics.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Adaptive-traffic-signal-control (ATSC) aims at minimizing traffic congestion which gives rise to a plethora of environmentally and socially harmful outcomes [1], [2], [3].

primary_category.justification: The paper addresses adaptive traffic signal control, which directly impacts transportation efficiency and indirectly reduces emissions, thus falling under Climate Change Mitigation.
primary_category.quote: Adaptive-traffic-signal-control (ATSC) aims at minimizing traffic congestion which gives rise to a plethora of environmentally and socially harmful outcomes.

secondary_categories.justification: The emphasis on handling variable traffic patterns and road network changes aligns with adapting to changing environmental conditions and infrastructure needs.
secondary_categories.quote: MuJAM, using both cyclic and acyclic constraints, outperforms domain-specific baselines as well as another transferable approach.

primary_sub_category.justification: The core of the paper is on optimizing traffic signal control, which is an intrinsic part of transportation.
primary_sub_category.quote: Index Terms—Adaptive traffic signal control, Transfer learning, Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, Joint Action Modeling, Model-Based Reinforcement Learning, Graph Neural Networks

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper indirectly supports adaptation by modeling traffic under varying conditions, akin to risk modeling.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: To test our claims, we introduce and evaluate various instantiations of MuJAM (and perform ablation studies) on zero-shot transfer settings involving road networks and non-stationary traffic distributions.

applications.justification: The paper's core application is the improvement and implementation of adaptive traffic signal control using reinforcement learning.
applications.quote: Adaptive-traffic-signal-control (ATSC) aims at minimizing traffic congestion which gives rise to a plethora of environmentally and socially harmful outcomes.

applications.justification: The method allows for zero-shot transfer to new systems without retraining, benefiting dynamic urban environments.
applications.quote: MuJAM enables the use of transferable approaches, which were limited to cyclic constraints until now (see § II), with acyclic constraints.
